1\. Context and constraints
===========================

The technical shape follows from the situation, not from habit. Five facts drive most decisions:  
Defaults follow the established stack for this practice: Next.js 15 (App Router), TypeScript in strict mode, Tailwind CSS 4, shadcn/ui on Radix primitives, TanStack Query for admin server state, React Hook Form with Zod, Supabase (Postgres, Auth, Row Level Security) and deployment on Vercel. Deviations are listed in section 3.

2\. Architecture overview
=========================

A **modular monolith**: one Next.js application containing the public site, the admin desk and the JSON API, talking to one Postgres database. There is no second service to deploy, monitor or secure. The next page shows the runtime picture.

2.1 Runtime view
----------------

![diagrams/architecture.png](data:image/png;base64,)  
Public pages are generated ahead of time (incremental static regeneration) and refreshed on demand when an admin publishes, so the common visitor path touches no database. Only the booking form, the status page and the admin app are dynamic.

2.2 Modules
-----------

| **Module** | **Responsibility** | **Owns tables** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| catalog | Services, packages, occasions, site settings | services, packages, occasions, site\_settings |
| portfolio | Portfolio items, media assets, testimonials, FAQs; image and video rendering | portfolio\_items, media\_assets, testimonials, faqs |
| booking | Request intake, availability, status machine, client tracking | bookings, booking\_events, blocked\_dates |
| quoting | Quotes, line items, acceptance, deposits | quotes, quote\_items, payments |
| notify | Email outbox, templates, retries, reminders | email\_outbox |
| content-legal | Legal documents, consent versions, enquiries | legal\_documents, enquiries |
| admin | Sign-in, scopes, dashboards | admin\_users |

Dependencies point inward: route handlers call services; services call repositories; repositories are the only code that touches the database client. A module may call another’s service, never its tables.

### Folder layout

src/  
app/  
(public)/ # home, services, portfolio, pricing, about, faq, contact, legal  
(public)/book/ # booking request (client component islands)  
booking/status/\[reference\]/page.tsx  
admin/ # dashboard, bookings, calendar, portfolio, content, team  
api/ # route handlers, one folder per resource  
modules/<module>/ # service.ts, repository.ts, schema.ts (Zod), types.ts  
lib/ # env.ts (validated), db.ts, auth.ts, errors.ts (RFC 7807), money.ts, dates.ts  
components/ui/ # shadcn primitives  
emails/ # React Email templates  
supabase/migrations/ # forward-only SQL, one file per change  
tests/ # unit, integration (RLS), e2e

3\. Technology decisions
========================

Each decision records what was chosen, what was rejected and the trigger that would reopen it.

| **ID** | **Decision** | **Alternatives considered** | **Reasoning** | **Reopen when** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ADR-01 | Next.js 15 App Router, TypeScript strict | Astro with islands; plain Vue or Svelte site | Needs a public site that is mostly static plus a dynamic booking flow and an admin app in one codebase. Astro would ship less JavaScript but needs a second stack for admin. Server Components keep client JavaScript within budget. | Admin is split out, or JS budget is missed after optimisation |
| ADR-02 | Supabase Postgres with RLS, Auth for admins only | Firebase; self-hosted Postgres; a custom Node API | Relational data with hard integrity rules (no overlapping confirmed jobs, frozen quotes). Postgres expresses those as constraints. RLS gives deny-by-default. | Need multi-region writes or vendor cost exceeds a self-hosted option |
| ADR-03 | Images on Cloudinary, signed uploads from admin | Supabase Storage with a resizing proxy; Vercel image optimisation only | Photography is the product. On-the-fly format and size negotiation (AVIF/WebP, DPR-aware widths) is the single biggest performance lever. Alt text and dimensions are stored in our database. | Monthly credits exceeded repeatedly |
| ADR-04 | Video as YouTube or Vimeo links, rendered as click-to-load facades; optional short hero loop from Cloudinary | Self-hosting MP4 or HLS | Streaming video from our own storage costs bandwidth and complexity. A facade (poster image first, iframe on tap) loads no third-party script until asked, keeps pages light and avoids cookies before consent. Privacy-enhanced embed hosts are used. | Client wants private or watermarked delivery (Phase 2 galleries) |
| ADR-05 | Email through Resend using a database outbox | Direct send inside request; SMTP | The outbox row is written in the same transaction as the booking, so a provider outage cannot lose a message. A cron retries with backoff. | Volume exceeds the free tier |
| ADR-06 | Arcjet for rate limiting and bot scoring | Upstash Ratelimit plus Turnstile; hand-rolled limiter | One vendor covers both; no visible CAPTCHA for normal visitors. Fails open for reads, falls back to a stricter in-app limit for the booking POST. | Free limits exceeded; swap to Upstash plus Turnstile (both have free tiers) |
| ADR-07 | Vercel for hosting; paid plan assumed | Cloudflare Pages or Workers; Netlify | Best fit for Next.js. The free Hobby tier is for personal, non-commercial use, so a business site needs a paid plan or another host. VERIFY current terms before launch. | Pricing or terms change |
| ADR-08 | No client accounts; tokenised links | Client login with email OTP | Most clients book once. A 256-bit random token, stored only as a hash, grants access to one booking. Less friction, less data held, nothing to reset. | Repeat clients or galleries need a library view |
| ADR-09 | Calendar integrity by an exclusion constraint | Application-level check; row locks; slot table | Two admins confirming at once cannot both win because the database refuses the second write. A check in code is a race; a constraint is not. | A second crew: scope the constraint per crew |
| ADR-10 | REST route handlers with shared Zod schemas; RFC 7807 errors | tRPC; GraphQL; Server Actions only | A stable, documented contract that can also serve a later mobile app or Paystack webhook. Zod schemas are shared by form and server, so validation cannot drift. | A mobile app needs generated clients |
| ADR-11 | Admin sign-in: Supabase Auth, password plus mandatory TOTP | Magic link only; social login | RLS helper requires an aal2 session, so a stolen password alone reads nothing. Authenticator apps work offline, which suits unreliable SMS and networks. | Hardware key requirement appears |
| ADR-12 | Cookieless analytics only | Google Analytics; ad pixels | Keeps version 1 free of consent banners and trackers (PRD FR-62). Product questions are answered by a few server-side funnel counters. | Marketing needs audience tools; add consent first |

4\. Booking lifecycle
=====================

The lifecycle is a state machine enforced in the database (a trigger rejects illegal moves), and mirrored in the service layer so the user sees a friendly message before the database has to refuse.  
![diagrams/booking-states.png](data:image/png;base64,)

4.1 Transitions
---------------

| **From** | **To** | **Triggered by** | **Guard** | **Side effects** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| new | reviewing | Admin opens the request | None | Timeline entry; first-response time recorded |
| reviewing | quoted | Admin sends a quote | Quote total equals sum of items; validity set | Quote frozen; email with status link |
| quoted | reviewing | Client asks for a change, or admin revises | Old quote becomes superseded | New draft version |
| quoted | accepted | Client accepts on status page | Quote still sent and not past validity; correct token | Quote accepted; admin emailed; deposit instructions shown |
| accepted | confirmed | Admin records deposit and sets the work window | Window present; no overlap with another confirmed job; deposit recorded | Date now public as unavailable; confirmation email; reminder scheduled |
| confirmed | completed | Admin marks delivered | Event date has passed | Timeline; optional review request (Phase 2) |
| quoted | expired | Daily job | valid\_until passed | Client emailed with a way to ask for a new quote |
| any open state | declined or cancelled | Admin, or client for cancel | Reason recorded | Date released if it was confirmed; client emailed |

4.2 Availability
----------------

Availability is **computed when read**, never kept as a counter that can drift. The public calendar asks one question: which dates in this range are unavailable? A date is unavailable if it falls in a blocked range, or if a confirmed photography or videography job starts on it (in Africa/Accra). The database view public\_unavailable\_dates returns dates only, never client details, and the endpoint is cached for 60 seconds.  
The picker is advisory. The booking endpoint re-checks the date on submit, and the only authoritative check is the exclusion constraint at confirmation: tstzrange(starts\_at, ends\_at) may not overlap for confirmed non-design bookings. The conflict surfaces to the admin as a clear message (HTTP 409, code window\_conflict). Ghana observes GMT all year, so there is no daylight saving case, but values are still stored as timestamptz and shown in Africa/Accra.

4.3 Pricing integrity
---------------------

Money is stored as integer pesewas. A quote is a draft until sent. A trigger refuses to send a quote whose total differs from the sum of its line items, and refuses any later change to the total, deposit or items. Revisions create a new version and mark the old one superseded. Public package prices are for display only; they are copied into a quote by an admin and then become frozen history.

====================

5.1 Creating a booking

5.2 Error contract
------------------

All errors use RFC 7807 problem details with a stable machine code, never a stack trace:  
HTTP/1.1 409 Conflict  
Content-Type: application/problem+json  
{ "type": "https://hephzibah.example/problems/date-unavailable",  
"title": "That date is no longer available",  
"status": 409, "code": "date\_unavailable",  
"detail": "Please choose another date or message us on WhatsApp.",  
"instance": "/api/bookings", "requestId": "req\_8f2c..." }

5.3 API specification
---------------------

Public and client endpoints:

| **Method and path** | **Caller** | **Request** | **Success** | **Errors** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GET /api/availability?from&to | Anyone | ISO dates, range up to 400 days | 200 { dates: \[\] }, cache 60 s | 422 invalid range |
| POST /api/bookings | Anyone | Header Idempotency-Key; body BookingRequest (kind, service, package?, occasion?, contact, date or deadline, brief, links, consent versions) | 201 { reference, statusUrl }; 200 on replay | 409 date\_unavailable; 422 field errors; 429 rate\_limited; 503 try\_later |
| POST /api/bookings/{ref}/quote/accept | Token holder | Authorization: Bearer <token>; body { quoteId } | 200 | 404 not\_found; 409 invalid\_state or quote\_unavailable |
| POST /api/bookings/{ref}/cancel | Token holder | Bearer token; body { reason? } | 200 | 404; 409 invalid\_state |
| POST /api/enquiries | Anyone | name, email, phone?, message, privacy version | 201 | 422; 429 |
| GET /api/health | Monitor | None | 200 { ok: true } (database round-trip) | 503 |

Admin endpoints (all require a valid session at aal2 and the scope shown; all return 403 with code forbidden otherwise):

| **Method and path** | **Scope** | **Purpose** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GET /api/admin/bookings | bookings | Cursor-paginated list; filters status, kind, from, to; search q (reference, name, email, phone) |
| GET /api/admin/bookings/{id} | bookings | Detail with timeline, quotes, payments |
| POST /api/admin/bookings/{id}/transition | bookings | { to, note?, startsAt?, endsAt? }; 409 window\_conflict or illegal\_transition |
| POST /api/admin/bookings/{id}/quotes | bookings | Create a draft quote with items; PATCH while draft; POST .../send freezes and emails |
| POST /api/admin/bookings/{id}/payments | bookings | Record a deposit or refund (append-only) |
| POST /api/admin/bookings/{id}/token/rotate | bookings | Issue a new access token and email it (revokes the old link) |
| GET, POST, DELETE /api/admin/blocked-dates | bookings | Manage unavailable ranges |
| POST /api/admin/uploads/sign | content | Returns a short-lived Cloudinary upload signature (type and size limited) |
| CRUD /api/admin/portfolio-items, /media | content | Publish requires the consent flag and alt text; triggers on-demand revalidation |
| CRUD /api/admin/services, /packages, /faqs, /testimonials | content | Catalogue and content |
| GET, PATCH /api/admin/enquiries | bookings | Inbox and status |
| PATCH /api/admin/settings; POST /api/admin/legal-documents | settings | Site settings; publish a new legal document version |
| GET, POST, PATCH /api/admin/team | team | Add or deactivate admins; assign scopes |

Scheduled jobs call GET /api/cron/{expire-quotes | send-email | reminders | retention} with Authorization: Bearer <CRON\_SECRET>: expiry daily; email retry every 10 minutes; reminders hourly; retention monthly.

5.4 Rate limits
---------------

| **Endpoint** | **Limit (per source)** | **On exceed** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| POST /api/bookings | 5 per 10 minutes, 20 per day | 429 with Retry-After; WhatsApp link shown |
| POST /api/enquiries | 3 per 10 minutes | 429 |
| Token endpoints | 10 per 10 minutes per reference | 429; repeated failures logged |
| Admin sign-in | 5 failed attempts per account per 15 minutes | Temporary lock; owner alerted |

6\. Roles and permissions
=========================

The model has two actors, matching the rest of the portfolio: **public** and **admin**. Admin capability is a list of scopes on the account, not a ladder of roles. A client is not a role; a token holder is simply a public caller proving knowledge of one booking’s secret.

| **Resource and action** | **Public** | **Token holder (own booking)** | **Admin: bookings** | **Admin: content** | **Admin: settings** | **Admin: team** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Read published portfolio, services, packages, FAQs, testimonials, legal | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Read unavailable dates (dates only) | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Create booking request or enquiry | Via API only | n/a | n/a | n/a | n/a | n/a |
| Read own booking and live quote | No | Yes | n/a | n/a | n/a | n/a |
| Accept quote; cancel own booking | No | Yes (state rules apply) | n/a | n/a | n/a | n/a |
| Read and change bookings, quotes, payments, enquiries, blocked dates | No | No | Yes | No | No | No |
| Create and edit drafts, publish portfolio, edit catalogue and FAQs | No | No | No | Yes | No | No |
| Edit site settings and legal documents | No | No | No | No | Yes | No |
| Add admins, set scopes | No | No | No | No | No | Yes |
| Read email outbox | No | No | No | No | No | Service role only |

Enforcement is layered: the UI hides what a user cannot do, the route handler checks the scope, and Row Level Security refuses the query regardless. Only the last layer is trusted. The anon key is public by design, so no public write policy exists: every public write goes through the server, where validation and rate limiting live.

7\. Threat model
================

Assets worth protecting, in order: client personal data and event details; the integrity of the calendar and quotes; admin access; the studio’s reputation (defacement, spam from our domain). The table lists the realistic threats for this system and what stops them.

| **Threat** | **Where** | **Mitigation** | **Residual** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Bulk fake bookings or enquiries | POST endpoints | Rate limits, bot scoring, honeypot, strict validation; no date held without a deposit | Some spam reaches inbox; admin can mark spam |
| Guessing booking references | Status page | Reference alone grants nothing; access needs a 256-bit token, stored hashed; token attempts rate limited | Negligible |
| Token leaked by forwarded email or shared link | Status page | Referrer-Policy: no-referrer, noindex, Cache-Control: no-store; token exposes one booking only; admin can rotate it; expires 90 days after the last activity | A forwarded link works until rotated; stated in the email |
| Admin account takeover | Admin sign-in | Mandatory TOTP; RLS requires aal2; lockout after failures; no shared accounts; deactivation instantly cuts access | Phished TOTP codes in real time; consider hardware keys later |
| Over-privileged service key exposed | Server | Service role key only in server environment variables; validated env module; never imported by client code (lint rule); rotated on any staff change | Leak through a compromised vendor build; rotate and audit |
| Cross-site scripting through client text | Admin views the brief | React escapes by default; no dangerouslySetInnerHTML for user text; legal Markdown is sanitised; strict Content Security Policy | Low |
| Spreadsheet formula injection | Admin CSV export | Cells beginning with =, +, -, @ are prefixed with an apostrophe on export | Low |
| Email abuse (our domain used to spam, header injection) | Outbox | Recipient is the validated booking email; templates are fixed; no user text in headers; SPF, DKIM, DMARC | Low |
| Unauthorised data access through RLS gaps | Database | RLS enabled on every table; default deny; policy tests in CI for each role; views that bypass RLS expose dates only | A new table without RLS; the CI check lists tables lacking it |
| Clickjacking and mixed content | All pages | frame-ancestors none, HSTS, upgrade insecure requests | None |
| Malicious or compromised third-party script | Browser | No third-party scripts in v1; video iframes load only on tap from privacy-enhanced hosts; subresource policy in CSP | Embedded video host is a trust dependency |
| Supply-chain compromise | Build | Lockfile, dependency alerts, pinned CI actions, review of new packages, minimal dependencies | Medium; accepted and monitored |
| Data loss or ransomware on the owner’s laptop | Operations | Data lives in managed services, not on laptops; backups with tested restore (section 12) | Low |

8\. Media pipeline
==================

9\. Observability
=================

| **Need** | **Approach** |
| --- | --- |
| Structured logs | JSON logs with a request ID that is also returned in error bodies; no personal data in logs beyond IDs |
| Errors | Error tracking on server and browser with personal data scrubbed |
| Uptime | External check on /api/health and the home page every 5 minutes, alerting the owner by email and WhatsApp-capable channel |
| Business funnel | Server-side counters: form opened, step reached, submitted, failed (by error code). No cookies, no user identifiers. |
| Email health | Outbox backlog and failure count on the admin dashboard; alert if the oldest pending message is older than 30 minutes |
| Performance | Field Core Web Vitals reported to the same cookieless store; lab runs in CI on the portfolio and booking pages |

11\. Test strategy
==================

| **Level** | **Tool** | **What must be covered** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Unit | Vitest | Zod schemas (including hostile input), money and date helpers, reference generator, state-transition table, token hashing |
| Database and policy | Local Supabase with SQL tests | Every invariant below, and a role matrix test: anon, token via server, admin without scope, admin with scope at aal1 and aal2, for every table |
| Integration | Vitest against local stack | Create-booking idempotency; quote send, accept, expire; email outbox retry |
| End to end | Playwright (mobile and desktop profiles) | Booking happy path for each kind; unavailable date refused; spam burst throttled; status link with wrong token; admin sign-in with TOTP; quote to confirmed; publish blocked without consent |
| Accessibility | axe in CI, manual screen-reader pass | Every public page and the booking flow; keyboard-only run; 200% zoom; reduced motion |
| Load | k6 | Booking POST and portfolio page against budgets |
| Security | Dependency audit, secret scanning, header check | No high-severity advisories at release; headers verified on production |

### Database invariants that have tests

| **Invariant** | **Mechanism** |
| --- | --- |
| Two confirmed crew jobs cannot overlap | Exclusion constraint on a time range |
| A confirmed job has a work window | Check constraint |
| Illegal status jumps are impossible | Trigger on status changes |
| A sent quote cannot change; its total equals its items | Triggers on quotes and quote\_items |
| A repeated submission creates one booking | Unique idempotency key plus conflict handling |
| Nothing unconsented is published | Check constraints on portfolio items and testimonials |
| Payments and timeline events are append-only | Update-blocking triggers |
| Anonymous visitors cannot read or write private tables, or call the booking function | RLS plus revoked function execution |
| Admin data needs a second factor | RLS helper requires an aal2 session |

The schema in this suite was applied to PostgreSQL 16 and these behaviours were exercised before writing this section; the scripts become the first tests in the repository.

12\. Environments, deployment and recovery
==========================================

| **Environment** | **Purpose** | **Data** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Local | Development with a local Supabase stack | Seed data only |
| Preview | One per pull request on the host; points at the staging database | Seed data only; never real clients |
| Production | Live site | Real data; access limited to the owner and named developers |

13\. Failure modes
==================

| **Failure** | **What the visitor sees** | **What the system does** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Database unavailable | Public pages still load from the static cache. Booking shows a friendly error and the WhatsApp link. | Health check fails and alerts the owner; requests are not queued blindly because they carry personal data |
| Email provider down | Nothing unusual; confirmation page already shown | Outbox rows stay pending and retry with backoff for 24 hours, then show on the dashboard as dead |
| Image host slow or down | Placeholders keep layout; text content intact | No change; alerts via uptime check on a sample image |
| Video host blocked on the visitor’s network | Poster with a link to open the video in a new tab | None |
| Bot service outage | Unaffected | Reads fail open; booking POST falls back to a strict in-app limit |
| Two admins confirm overlapping jobs | n/a | Database refuses the second; message names the conflicting window |
| Admin loses authenticator device | n/a | Owner resets that user’s factor after an identity check; recovery codes issued at setup |
| Cron job missed | n/a | Jobs are idempotent and catch up on the next run; dashboard shows last run time |

14\. Cost and upgrade plan
==========================

The practice’s default is free tier first, with a stated trigger to move up. For this project two triggers are already met at launch, which is why the PRD flags them as risks.

| **Service** | **Starting assumption** | **Upgrade trigger** | **Note** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Hosting (Vercel) | Paid plan from launch | Already met: free tier is for non-commercial use. VERIFY terms. | Alternative: another host for the Next.js app |
| Database (Supabase) | Paid plan from launch | Already met in practice: free projects can pause after inactivity, which a booking site cannot tolerate. VERIFY. | Fallback: free plan plus keep-alive cron and a tested restore |
| Images (Cloudinary) | Free plan | Monthly credits exceeded two months running | Reduce delivered widths first |
| Email (Resend) | Free plan | More than about 100 emails a day or 3,000 a month | Volume here is far below this |
| Bot and rate limit (Arcjet) | Free plan | Limits exceeded | Swap for Upstash plus Turnstile |
| Error tracking | Free plan | Event quota exceeded | Sample or filter noise first |

Prices and free-tier limits change often. Confirm each vendor’s current plan before committing the budget.
